# Corpus coverage matrix

30 cases across 4 categories. Generated by hand from each case's `case.yaml`
`covers` block; `internal/repositoryquality`'s
`TestCorpusCoverageDocumentReferencesRealCaseIDs` guards this document
against drifting out of sync with the corpus (every case ID below must
appear here). See `coverage-exceptions.yaml` for gaps documented instead of
silently claimed.

## Case count by category

| Category | Cases |
| --- | ---: |
| gitleaks | 7 |
| github-actions | 10 |
| compose | 7 |
| integrated | 6 |
| **Total** | **30** |

## Report formats and profiles

Every success case's golden pair covers both `expected.json` (schema v2) and
`expected.sarif` (SARIF 2.1.0); terminal, HTML, and Mermaid rendering are
covered by their own package-level tests (`internal/reporters/terminal`,
`internal/reporters/html`, `internal/reporters/mermaid`), not this corpus.

| Profile | Cases |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` (default) | 25 cases |
| `production` (explicit) | integrated-gitleaks-compose-published |
| `local` (explicit) | integrated-isolated-lower-impact |
| `auto` selected via `config_file` (`.credscope.yml`, `gitleaks.path_prefix`) | gitleaks-path-prefix-normalization |
| `production` selected via `config_file` (`.credscope.yml`, `ignore.*`) | integrated-allowlist-ignore-config |

`staging` and `ci` profiles are not explicitly exercised by any case; see
`coverage-exceptions.yaml` is not required for this since profile selection
itself is a config/analysis-layer concern already covered by
`internal/profile`'s own unit tests, not a corpus-specific gap.

Additional internal structural edges (`detected_in`, `belongs_to`,
`triggered_by`, `has_permission`, `uses_environment`, `runs_action`,
`mounts_volume`, `calls_workflow`) appear incidentally in rendered graph
output as ordinary structural scaffolding; `has_permission`,
`uses_environment`, and `mounts_volume` are additionally named explicitly in
some cases' `covers.edges` (gha-elevated-permissions,
integrated-gitleaks-actions-higher-impact,
compose-bind-mount-and-docker-socket) where they are directly relevant to
that case's reviewed scenario. `runs_action` is additionally named
explicitly by gha-local-composite-action-resolved, where it carries
`structural_call_only` evidence from a workflow-step call-site node to a
resolved repository-local composite action's canonical `composite_action`
node (Phase CA1). `gha-composite-action-confirmed-input-flow` additionally
covers `runs_action`, `explicitly_forwarded_to`, and confirmed call-specific
binding-to-usage reachability introduced in Phase CA2.
`gha-nested-composite-action-resolved` additionally covers a second,
composite-action-internal `runs_action`/`structural_call_only` edge —
introduced in Phase CA3A — from one canonical composite action to a further
canonical composite action its own internal step resolves to, proving the
CA1 workflow-call-site structural edge and the CA3A action-internal
structural edge coexist without either becoming traversable.
`gha-nested-composite-action-confirmed-input-flow` additionally covers Phase
CA3B: a second, call-specific `explicitly_forwarded_to` hop from a parent
composite action's own confirmed input-usage node to a nested composite
action's own confirmed input-binding node, and onward to that nested
action's own confirmed internal-usage node — extending CA2's root
binding/usage chain one nesting level deeper while CA1's and CA3A's
structural `runs_action` edges continue to coexist, unchanged and
non-traversable.

## Secret-safety coverage

| Property | Covered by |
| --- | --- |
| Secret/Match never in output (raw, JSON-escaped, URL-encoded, base64) | every case with `inputs.gitleaks` set, enforced on every render by the corpus runner; gitleaks-secret-and-match-never-in-output specifically stresses every redacted field |
| Stable fingerprinting without storing raw value | gitleaks-normal-finding, gitleaks-missing-optional-fields |
| Repository-root confinement (finding paths) | gitleaks-repository-root-confinement (negative control) |
| Absolute-path-prefix normalization | gitleaks-path-prefix-normalization |
| Duplicate/repeated finding handling | gitleaks-multiple-and-duplicate-findings |

## Determinism coverage

| Property | Covered by |
| --- | --- |
| Byte-identical output across two in-process analysis runs | every case, enforced unconditionally by the corpus runner (`Execute`), not opt-in |
| YAML map key ordering does not change semantic output | gha-map-ordering-determinism |
| Deterministic ordering at multi-credential scale | integrated-multi-finding-deterministic-ordering |
| Discovery order is stable and ID-sorted | internal/repositoryquality's TestCorpusDiscoveryOrderIsDeterministic |
